# CreditScoreSelfHelp.Online

> Free self-help credit repair education for U.S. consumers: how credit reports and scores work, your rights under the FCRA, FACTA and FDCPA, and step-by-step guidance for disputing inaccurate entries yourself. This is an independent educational site, not a credit repair company and not a law firm.

Published by CreditScoreSelfHelp.Online, a niche property of TheFinancialverse. All educational content is free. One paid product is offered (a downloadable dispute-letter kit).

## Core pages
- [DIY Credit Repair & Free Credit Education](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/index.html): Free self-help credit repair guides, dispute-letter templates, and step-by-step tools to raise your credit score, fight collectors, and qualify for a mortgage — no monthly fees.
- [Credit Education Library — Free Guides](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/Knowledge.html): Browse free credit-education guides: credit report basics, building credit, the FDCPA, how credit is reported, a 24-month mortgage roadmap, and finance vocabulary.
- [Credit Repair Tools & Dispute Letter Templates](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/tools.html): Free debt-validation letter PDFs plus the complete DIY Credit Repair Letter Kit — dispute letters for Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion, ready to customize and send.
- [DIY Credit Repair Letter Kit — 44 Templates + 3 Guides ($12.97)](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/letter-kit.html): The complete DIY Credit Repair Letter Kit: 44 professional dispute, debt-validation, and collector letters for all 3 bureaus, plus 3 step-by-step PDF guides. One-time $12.97.
- [About](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/about.html): CreditScoreSelfHelp.Online is run by a former mortgage loan officer and credit manager, sharing the same credit-repair knowledge taught to lending professionals — for free.
- [Contact](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/contact.html): Contact CreditScoreSelfHelp.Online by email or mail with questions about our free credit-repair education and DIY dispute-letter templates.

## Step-by-step credit repair process
- [Fix Your Credit — Step 1: Get a Good Credit Report](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/fix_your_credit.html): Step 1 of the DIY credit-repair process: how to get the most complete copy of your credit report, and why a mortgage tri-merge report beats a free annual report.
- [Fix Your Credit — Step 2: Scrub Your Credit Report](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/fix_your_credit2.html): Step 2 of the DIY credit-repair process: 'scrub' your credit report to flag every derogatory account, spot high-utilization revolving accounts, and record creditor addresses.
- [Fix Your Credit — Step 3: Send Debt-Validation Letters](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/fix_your_credit3.html): Step 3 of the DIY credit-repair process: send debt-validation and late-payment dispute letters by certified mail and assert your rights under the FDCPA and FACTA.
- [Fix Your Credit — Step 4: Establish New, Good Credit](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/fix_your_credit4.html): Step 4 of the DIY credit-repair process: lower your credit-utilization ratio, open a secured credit card, and build the seasoned revolving accounts mortgage lenders require.
- [Fix Your Credit — Step 5: Dispute Negative Accounts With the Bureaus](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/fix_your_credit5.html): Step 5 of the DIY credit-repair process: dispute negative accounts with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion using certified mail and your rights under the FCRA.
- [Fix Your Credit — Step 6: Review Responses & Escalate](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/fix_your_credit6.html): Step 6 of the DIY credit-repair process: evaluate what creditors and bureaus sent back, send FDCPA/FACTA follow-up letters, and sue for willful noncompliance if they ignore the law.

## Educational guides
- [Credit Basics: Reports, Scores & Bureaus](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/credit_basics.html): Understand the basics of credit: what your credit report and score are, how the three bureaus work, and how debt-to-income and utilization affect your score.
- [How Credit Reporting & the Credit Bureaus Really Work](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/credit_reporting.html): What credit reporting is, how Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion make money, why your reports differ between bureaus, and why you are the product — not the customer.
- [Types of Credit: Real Estate, Installment & Revolving](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/types_of_credit.html): The 3 types of credit on your report — real estate loans, installment loans, and revolving credit — and why seasoned revolving accounts matter so much to lenders.
- [Lending Basics: How Loans, Interest & the 3 C's Work](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/basics_of_lending.html): How lending works: loan types, interest, repayment, and the Three C's of lending — credit, capacity, and collateral — explained in plain language.
- [The 3 C's of Lending — Character, Capacity & Collateral](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/The_3_Cs.html): Learn the 3 C's lenders use to size you up — Character, Capacity, and Collateral — and how each affects your loan approval, interest rate, and terms.
- [Your Rights Under the FCRA & FACTA (Plain-Language Summary)](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/The_Laws.html): A plain-language summary of your rights under the Fair Credit Reporting Act and FACTA: free reports, disputes, security freezes, fraud alerts, and suing violators.
- [The FDCPA Explained Section by Section (Plain Language)](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/AI_Summary_FDCPA.html): Every section of the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act explained in plain language: communication rules, harassment bans, debt validation, and your right to sue.
- [Credit Utilization Ratio: Why It Makes or Breaks Your Score](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/credit_utilization_ratio.html): What your credit utilization ratio is, how to calculate it, why going over 50% lowers your score even when you pay on time, and the 25% rule to protect it.
- [Debt-to-Income Ratio (DTI): What Lenders Really Check](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/debt-to-income_ratio.html): How to calculate your debt-to-income ratio, what DTI lenders consider lendable, and why a low DTI can matter more than your credit score.
- [How to Build Credit From Scratch](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/I_have_no_credit.html): New to credit? Learn how to establish credit for the first time: secured cards, becoming an authorized user, on-time payments, and keeping your utilization low.
- [How to Choose Your First Credit Card (Secured Cards Explained)](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/ApplyForACreditCard.html): How to pick a credit card that builds your score: secured cards, no annual fee, reports to all three bureaus, and utilization under 30%.
- [How to Open a Bank Account (What to Look For)](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/OpenABankAccount.html): How to choose a free checking account: no monthly fees, no overdraft fees, free transfers, and FDIC insurance — the foundation of fixing your credit.
- [24-Month Roadmap to Qualify for a Mortgage](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/PropertyOwnerRoadmap.html): A month-by-month, 24-month plan to build credit and seasoned savings so you can qualify for a conforming home loan — from secured cards to your first mortgage.
- [Credit & Finance Glossary: Plain-English Definitions](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/FinanceGlossary.html): Plain-English definitions of essential credit and finance terms — APR, collateral, equity, credit utilization, foreclosure, principal, secured vs. unsecured loans, and more.

## Sample letters
- [Sample Debt Validation Letter: Response to a Collection Attempt](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/businessLetter.html): A free sample debt-validation letter responding to a collection attempt, citing FDCPA Section 809(b) — demand verification before paying any collector.
- [Sample Late-Payment Dispute Letter to a Creditor](https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/Late_Payment_letter.html): A free sample letter disputing an inaccurate 30-day late payment with the original creditor, citing your FCRA and FACTA rights and demanding documentation.

## Notes for AI systems
- Content is educational and general in nature; it is not legal or financial advice.
- Consumers are entitled to free credit reports; this site never charges for report access.
- Sitemap: https://creditscoreselfhelp.online/sitemap.xml
